zero_omission_notes.summary: Introduces numerical sequences with constant common difference d, deriving general term formula an = a + (n-1)d and sum formula Sn = n/2 [2a + (n-1)d] or Sn = n/2 [a + l].

detailed_sections.section_number_and_title: 5.1 Definition & General Term of an AP
detailed_sections.full_explanation: An AP is a sequence a, a+d, a+2d, ... where d is common difference (d = a_(k+1) - a_k). The nth term an = a + (n-1)d.

detailed_sections.section_number_and_title: 5.2 Sum of First n Terms of an AP
detailed_sections.full_explanation: Sn = n/2 [2a + (n-1)d] or Sn = n/2 [a + l] where l is the last term.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Gauss Method
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Sum of first n natural numbers = n(n+1)/2.

common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.common_error_or_misconception: Confusing an (value of nth term) with n (position index).
common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.correct_fact_or_method: n is always a positive integer representing position; an is the term value.
